newsitem.title: MEXICO: Dina says refinances $125 mln Motor Coach.
newsitem.headline: Dina says refinances $125 mln Motor Coach.

text.p: Commercial vehicle manufacturer Consorcio G Grupo Dina said on Friday that it refinanced $125 million in revolving debt held by its U.S. subsidiary Motor Coach Industries International, with a banking syndicate headed by First Chicago Bank and National Bank of Detroit.
"Debt repayment conditions underwent no substantial changes in amount, term and rate, compared to the previous revolving debt held with a syndicate led by Citibank," a news release from Dina said.
The refinancing will allow Motor Coach to send up to $30 million to Grupo Dina for its Mexican operations, mainly for working capital, of which it had already transferred $20 million.
Dina said the amount had been approved by Motor Coach promissory-note holders.
Dina also said its truck and bus division had obtained credit lines of $15 million and $20 million, respectively, granted by Mexico's Foreign Trade Bank (Bancomext).
These loans were to finance export sales to Latin America and the United States.

The company also said it had made a back-dated adjustment of 43 million pesos to its financial statements for the first half of the year, corresponding to the possible loss entailed in selling its Estrella Blanca bus portfolio to Arrendadora Financiera Dina, its leasing arm.
"Although the negotiations have not been finalized, this item is considered sufficient to absorb any loss that may arise from this operation," the news release said.
